html:
The Wiwa are an Indigenous people of the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta, the isolated coastal mountain range of northern Colombia. They speak a Chibchan language and share the mountain with the Kogi, the Arhuaco and the Kankuamo.

These four peoples see themselves as heirs of the Tairona, who built stone towns and terraces in the Sierra before the Spanish conquest. They hold that the mountain is the heart of the world and that their spiritual leaders, the mamos, must care for it. In the late 1900s the Wiwa were caught between guerrillas, paramilitaries and drug growers, and many were killed or forced out. Today they live in reserves on the south-eastern side of the Sierra.
